In this week you will learn the fundamental **building blocks of R**: how data is stored, organised, and accessed. These concepts underlie everything that comes later.

> **Tip:** The [Basics in Coding](coding_basics.html) reference page gives you a quick-lookup summary of all syntax covered this week — keep it open while working in RStudio.

### Quiz 1: Vectors
<span id="quiz-done-w1_q_vectors" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span>

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does <code>length(c(9, 3, 7, 2))</code> return?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v1" id="v1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="v1a">2</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v1" id="v1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="v1b">4</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v1" id="v1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="v1c">9</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v1" id="v1d"><label class="form-check-label" for="v1d">1</label></div>
    <div id="v1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> Why does <code>sum(c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE))</code> return <code>3</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v2" id="v2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="v2a">Because the vector has 3 elements</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v2" id="v2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="v2b">Because R treats TRUE as 1 and FALSE as 0 — sum() therefore counts the TRUE values</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v2" id="v2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="v2c">Because sum() only counts the first three elements</label></div>
    <div id="v2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does <code>y[y &lt; 5]</code> return when <code>y &lt;- c(9, 3, 7, 2)</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v3" id="v3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="v3a">9 7</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v3" id="v3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="v3b">3 2</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v3" id="v3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="v3c">TRUE FALSE TRUE TRUE</label></div>
    <div id="v3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 4:</strong> What happens when data types are mixed in a vector, e.g. <code>c(TRUE, "FALSE", 3)</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v4" id="v4a"><label class="form-check-label" for="v4a">R throws an error</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v4" id="v4b"><label class="form-check-label" for="v4b">Each element keeps its own type</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="v4" id="v4c"><label class="form-check-label" for="v4c">All elements are converted to the lowest common type (here: character)</label></div>
    <div id="v4-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkVektorQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="vektor-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
```

### Quiz 2: Matrices
<span id="quiz-done-w1_q_matrices" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span>

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does <code>dim(X)</code> return for <code>X &lt;- matrix(1:6, nrow=2, ncol=3)</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m1" id="m1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="m1a">6</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m1" id="m1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="m1b">2 3</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m1" id="m1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="m1c">3 2</label></div>
    <div id="m1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What is the difference between <code>cbind()</code> and <code>rbind()</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m2" id="m2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="m2a">No difference – both do the same thing</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m2" id="m2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="m2b">cbind() joins vectors as columns, rbind() as rows</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m2" id="m2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="m2c">cbind() only works for numbers, rbind() for all types</label></div>
    <div id="m2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does <code>X[2, ]</code> return?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m3" id="m3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="m3a">The element in row 2, column 0</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m3" id="m3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="m3b">All elements of the second row</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="m3" id="m3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="m3c">All elements of the second column</label></div>
    <div id="m3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkMatrixQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="matrix-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
```

---

### Quiz 3: Lists
<span id="quiz-done-w1_q_lists" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span>

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is the difference between <code>List1["color"]</code> and <code>List1[["color"]]</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl1" id="wl1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl1a">No difference – both return the same value</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl1" id="wl1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl1b"><code>List1["color"]</code> returns a list of length 1; <code>List1[["color"]]</code> returns the content (the vector) directly</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl1" id="wl1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl1c"><code>List1[["color"]]</code> returns a list; <code>List1["color"]</code> returns the content</label></div>
    <div id="wl1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> How do you access the <strong>second position</strong> of the first element of <code>List2 &lt;- list(c("blue", "red"), 5, TRUE)</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl2" id="wl2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl2a"><code>List2[1][2]</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl2" id="wl2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl2b"><code>List2[[1]][2]</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl2" id="wl2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl2c"><code>List2$1[2]</code></label></div>
    <div id="wl2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> How do you delete the third element from a list?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl3" id="wl3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl3a"><code>List2[3] &lt;- FALSE</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl3" id="wl3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl3b"><code>List2[[3]] &lt;- NULL</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="wl3" id="wl3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="wl3c"><code>rm(List2[[3]])</code></label></div>
    <div id="wl3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkListQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="list-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
```

### Quiz 4: Dataframes
<span id="quiz-done-w1_q_dataframes" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span>

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is the most important difference between a dataframe and a matrix?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d1" id="d1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="d1a">Dataframes can be larger than matrices</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d1" id="d1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="d1b">Dataframes can contain different data types in different columns; matrices only one type throughout</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d1" id="d1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="d1c">Matrices always have column names, dataframes do not</label></div>
    <div id="d1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> How many fruits does <code>Fruit &lt;- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)</code> contain, and which function do you use?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d2" id="d2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="d2a">2, with <code>length(Fruit)</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d2" id="d2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="d2b">3, with <code>sum(Fruit)</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d2" id="d2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="d2c">5, with <code>sum(Fruit)</code></label></div>
    <div id="d2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does <code>merge(Students, Full_Names)</code> do by default?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d3" id="d3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="d3a">All rows of both dataframes are merged; missing values filled with NA</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d3" id="d3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="d3b">Only rows that appear in both dataframes are kept (Inner Join)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="d3" id="d3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="d3c">The dataframes are stacked on top of each other</label></div>
    <div id="d3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkDfQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="df-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
```
